plugins.name: dgc-templates
plugins.summary: Short writing templates for a status note, a decision, a plan, and a letter.
plugins.long_summary: DGC templates are original instructions for plain documents. Each one tells the model which sections to write and what to leave out. They do not include another product's template files.
plugins.verification: Package structure checked; model behaviour depends on its tool support.

plugins.name: dgc-plugin-management
plugins.summary: Find, install, and turn off DGC plugins and their skills.
plugins.long_summary: Use this when a task needs a plugin that is not connected yet, or when a skill from an installed plugin should stay off. It describes DGC's own plugin list, sign-in, and skill switches.
plugins.verification: Package structure checked; model behaviour depends on its tool support.

plugins.name: composio
plugins.summary: Connect your Composio account to DGC. Authorize and manage apps in Composio.
plugins.verification: DGC browser handoff verified. A user confirmed Figma connection in Composio. Individual app setup from DGC settings is not supported; use Composio Connect Apps. Authenticated tool execution in DGC remains unverified.
plugins.requirements: A Composio For You account, browser consent, and Node.js/npm for DGC’s existing remote MCP bridge. Composio handles app credentials and executes app requests in its cloud, including when your model runs locally.

metadata.long_summary: Connect an existing Composio account or create one in your browser. Open Composio For You → Connect Apps to authorize and manage your apps. Then return to DGC and ask it to use them. App permissions, account selection and revocation are managed in Composio or the provider’s account settings.

plugins.name: google-workspace
plugins.summary: Choose Gmail, Calendar, Contacts and Drive. Requires Google Cloud setup and Workspace MCP preview access.
plugins.setup_instructions: Google requires Workspace MCP preview access, a Cloud project with the selected APIs enabled, and your own OAuth client. DGC does not have a registered Google OAuth client. Installation saves only the selected server definitions; it does not sign you in or start these servers. Complete Google’s setup, then configure credentials in MCP servers. Google account access is not supplied by Codex or inherited from ChatGPT.

metadata.long_summary: Connect selected Google Workspace services through Google’s published MCP endpoints. Setup is required before DGC can access account data.

plugins.block_reason: Requires Google Workspace MCP preview access and a registered OAuth client. DGC has neither configured; these presets do not provide a working sign-in.
plugins.verification: Unavailable in DGC

plugins.name: zapier
plugins.summary: Use the apps and actions connected to your own Zapier account.
plugins.requirements: In Zapier MCP, add a server for Other, open Connect, and generate a connection token. Copy the token itself into DGC. Manage your apps and tools in Zapier.
plugins.verification: Documented setup implemented. Complete account sign-in and a tool call to verify access for your account.

metadata.long_summary: Use the apps and actions connected to your own Zapier account. In Zapier MCP, add a server for Other, open Connect, and generate a connection token. Copy the token itself into DGC. Manage your apps and tools in Zapier.

plugins.summary: Run the scenarios you configure in your Make account.
plugins.requirements: Connect your Make account in the browser and choose the organization and scopes. The Run your scenarios scope covers its active and on-demand scenarios. Manage scenarios and app credentials in Make.
plugins.verification: Documented setup implemented. Complete account sign-in and a tool call to verify access for your account.

plugins.name: n8n
plugins.summary: Use selected workflows on n8n Cloud or your own n8n instance.
plugins.requirements: In your n8n instance, enable Settings → Instance-level MCP, expose the workflows you want to use, and copy the server URL. Choose browser sign-in or a personal access token. With Remote SSH, local addresses refer to the machine running DGC.
plugins.verification: Documented setup implemented. Complete account sign-in and a tool call to verify access for your account.

With Remote SSH, local addresses refer to the machine running DGC.

plugins.name: arcade
plugins.summary: Connect a gateway containing the tools you select in Arcade.
plugins.requirements: Create an MCP Gateway in Arcade, select Arcade Auth and the tools to expose, then copy its gateway URL. Sign in with your own Arcade account. Manage tools and provider authorization in Arcade. This setup supports Arcade Cloud gateways.
plugins.verification: Documented setup implemented. Complete account sign-in and a tool call to verify access for your account.
